elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause grants Client ownership only of deliverables prepared by TrueLink “under the Support Services.” It does not cover deliverables created for Client under other services or arrangements.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Ownership is limited to work product prepared “under the Support Services,” which is narrower than all work product created for Client.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all of Vendor’s rights in deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: TrueLink presently assigns all right, title and interest in defined Work Product, but that definition includes only deliverables prepared under the Support Services.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all of Vendor’s rights in work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The assignment is express but limited to Work Product prepared under the Support Services, rather than all work product created for Client.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of all Vendor pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: The existing clause reserves TrueLink’s rights in the Interface, and the new clause implies that embedded TrueLink Intellectual Property remains licensable, but there is no general reservation of all pre-existing TrueLink IP.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: A licence is granted for TrueLink Intellectual Property embedded in defined Work Product, but Work Product is limited to materials prepared under the Support Services and therefore may not encompass all deliverables.

elements.element: The embedded-Vendor-IP licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly stated to be “perpetual.”

elements.element: The embedded-Vendor-IP licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly stated to be “irrevocable.”

elements.element: The embedded-Vendor-IP licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly stated to be “royalty-free.”

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Client expressly retains all right, title and interest in all data of Client and its borrowers, loan applicants, customers and brokers submitted to or processed through the Interface or Web Site. The earlier nonexclusive Credit Data licence does not transfer ownership.

elements.element: No jointly owned intellectual property is created.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that “no jointly owned intellectual property is created hereunder.”

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause reserves TrueLink’s rights only in the Interface and does not expressly reserve ownership of generic tools generally.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: No operative language reserves TrueLink’s ownership of know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence covering the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Client receives ownership of deliverables prepared under the Support Services and a licence to embedded TrueLink IP, but there is no licence covering all deliverables without the Support Services limitation.

elements.element: Customer’s rights in the deliverables are perpetual.
elements.evidence: Ownership of the covered Work Product is not term-limited, and the licence to embedded TrueLink IP is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: Customer’s rights in the deliverables are irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The Work Product assignment is unconditional, and the embedded-IP licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer’s rights in the deliverables are worldwide.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly worldwide, and Client’s ownership of the covered Work Product has no geographic limitation.

elements.element: Customer’s rights in the deliverables are royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly royalty-free, and no royalty applies to Client’s ownership of the covered Work Product.

elements.element: Customer may use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Client owns the covered Work Product, and the embedded-IP licence expressly permits use.

elements.element: Customer may modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Client owns the covered Work Product, and the embedded-IP licence expressly permits modification.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Client may license its owned Work Product, and the embedded-IP licence expressly permits sublicensing of embedded TrueLink IP.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its deliverable rights for its business.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence expressly permits the licensed rights to be exercised as part of the Work Product in Client’s business.

result.reason: Neither level is complete. The preferred position is underinclusive because ownership, assignment and the embedded-IP licence are limited to Work Product prepared under the Support Services, and there is no general reservation of all TrueLink pre-existing IP. The fallback fails because generic tools and know-how are not expressly reserved and the deliverables licence is similarly under-scoped. The added language otherwise preserves TrueLink’s Interface ownership and the existing commercial terms without an express contradiction.
